eras.title: The Ranchi Boy
eras.summary: A goalkeeper who was pushed into wicketkeeping, a ticket collector on the Kharagpur platform, a late bloomer who missed every youth pipeline and then could not be ignored.

eras.title: Breaking Through
eras.summary: Run out for nought on debut, then 148 against Pakistan and 183 not out against Sri Lanka inside a year. Long hair, big sixes, and the No.1 ODI batting ranking.

eras.title: Captain Cool
eras.summary: Handed a young side for the first World T20 and won it. Then the CB Series in Australia, the Test captaincy, No.1 in Tests, an Asia Cup and CSK's first IPL title.

eras.title: The World Champion
eras.summary: The six at the Wankhede, 224 against Australia, a 4–0 Test sweep and a rain-soaked Champions Trophy final at Edgbaston that completed the only ICC treble.

eras.title: The Finisher
eras.summary: Retired from Tests mid-series, led India to another World Cup semi-final, won the Asia Cup, then quietly handed the white-ball captaincy to Virat Kohli.

eras.title: Senior Statesman
eras.summary: CSK's comeback title, 10,000 ODI runs, the Padma Bhushan in army uniform, and a last international innings that ended in a run-out at Old Trafford.

eras.title: Beyond International Cricket
eras.summary: Retirement announced at 19:29 on Independence Day. Two more IPL titles with Chennai, a Hall of Fame cap, and a life of bikes, farms and the Ranchi he never left.

events.title: Born in Ranchi
events.text: Mahendra Singh Dhoni is born to Pan Singh, a junior manager at MECON, and Devaki Devi, the youngest of three children after Narendra and Jayanti. The family lives in the MECON colony at Shyamali.
events.source: ICC Hall of Fame profile; BCCI player profile

events.title: Goalkeeper first, wicketkeeper second
events.text: A football goalkeeper and badminton player at school, he is sent to try wicketkeeping by games teacher Keshav Banerjee. He keeps for the Commando Cricket Club (1995–98) and is picked for Vinoo Mankad Trophy under-16s in 1997–98.

events.title: First-class debut for Bihar
events.text: At 18 he makes his Ranji Trophy debut for Bihar against Assam, scoring 68 not out in the second innings. When Jharkhand is carved out of Bihar in November 2000 he becomes one of the new state's first players.

events.title: Ticket collector at Kharagpur
events.text: Through the sports quota he works as a Travelling Ticket Examiner at Kharagpur railway station from 2001 to 2003, playing for the Railways in domestic cricket. He later says the job taught him to deal with people; he left it to chase a career the selectors had not yet noticed.

events.title: Noticed at last
events.place: Deodhar Trophy and Duleep Trophy, East Zone
events.text: Hitting for East Zone in the 2002–03 Deodhar Trophy and the 2003–04 Duleep Trophy final brings him to the attention of the BCCI's Talent Resource Development Wing, whose scout PC Poddar files the report that reaches the national selectors.

events.title: India A in Kenya
events.place: Nairobi, tri-series with Pakistan A and Kenya
events.text: Two centuries against Pakistan A, 120 and 119 not out, and a tournament aggregate above 350 runs leave the selectors with no excuse. Sourav Ganguly and Ravi Shastri both push for him.

events.title: ODI debut — run out for 0
events.text: He walks out at No.7 and is run out without scoring on his first appearance for India. He makes 12 and 7 not out in the remaining two games of the series.

events.title: 148 against Pakistan
events.text: Promoted to No.3 in only his fifth ODI, he hits 148 off 123 balls with 15 fours and 4 sixes, the highest score by an Indian wicketkeeper at the time. India win by 58 runs.
events.source: ESPNcricinfo scorecard, 2nd ODI, India v Pakistan 2005

events.title: 183 not out — still the highest ODI score by a wicketkeeper
events.text: Chasing 299 he comes in at No.3 and hits 183 not out off 145 balls (15 fours, 10 sixes), the highest score ever in an ODI chase at the time and still the highest by a wicketkeeper in the format.
events.source: ESPNcricinfo scorecard; ICC Hall of Fame

events.title: Test debut
events.text: In a rain-ruined Test he scores 30 off 51 balls and takes a catch and a stumping. Four weeks later in Faisalabad he makes his first Test century, 148 off 153 balls, against Pakistan.

events.title: No.1 ODI batter in the world
events.text: Sixteen months after debut he tops the ICC ODI batting rankings, the first Indian to do so, displacing Ricky Ponting.

events.title: T20I debut
events.text: India's first ever T20I. Dhoni is stumped for 0 off 2 balls; India win by six wickets. He will play 98 more.

events.title: Named captain for the first World T20
events.text: With Tendulkar, Dravid and Ganguly opting out of the inaugural ICC World Twenty20, the 26-year-old is handed a young squad. The appointment comes months after India's first-round World Cup exit in the Caribbean.

events.title: World T20 champions
events.text: India 157/5; Pakistan need 13 off the last over with one wicket left. Dhoni gives the ball to Joginder Sharma over Harbhajan Singh. Misbah-ul-Haq scoops to short fine leg, Sreesanth holds it, India win by five runs.

events.title: First ODI as captain
events.text: Rahul Dravid steps down and Dhoni is appointed ODI captain. His first match in charge is washed out; India lose the series 2–4 but the rebuild has begun.

events.title: CB Series won in Australia
events.text: After the acrimonious Sydney Test, Dhoni's 'young legs' selection policy pays off: India beat Australia in both finals (Sydney and Brisbane) to win a tri-series on Australian soil for the first time.

events.title: First Test as captain
events.text: Standing in for the injured Anil Kumble, he wins his first Test in charge by eight wickets inside three days. He takes over full-time when Kumble retires in November 2008 during the home series against Australia, which India win 2–0.

events.title: Bought by Chennai Super Kings
events.text: Chennai pay US$1.5 million, the highest price at the inaugural auction, to make him their captain. CSK reach the first IPL final, losing to Rajasthan Royals off the last ball.

events.title: Padma Shri
events.text: Awarded the Padma Shri, having already received the Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna for 2007–08, India's highest sporting honour.
events.source: Padma Awards, Ministry of Home Affairs

events.title: India No.1 in Tests for the first time
events.text: An innings win at the Brabourne Stadium takes India to the top of the ICC Test rankings for the first time. They stay there for 20 months.

events.title: CSK's first IPL title
events.place: DY Patil Stadium, Navi Mumbai, v Mumbai Indians
events.text: Suresh Raina's 57 not out and a 22-run win give Chennai their first title. Dhoni has promoted himself and played the long game all tournament; CSK qualify on the final league day.

events.title: Asia Cup champions
events.text: India win the Asia Cup for the first time since 1995, beating Sri Lanka by 81 runs in the final. In September CSK add the Champions League T20 in Johannesburg.

events.title: World Cup champions — the six at the Wankhede
events.text: Chasing 275, India are 114/3 when Dhoni promotes himself above the in-form Yuvraj Singh. He makes 91 not out off 79 balls and finishes it with a six over long-on off Nuwan Kulasekara with 10 balls to spare. Player of the match. India's first World Cup in 28 years.

events.title: Back-to-back IPL titles
events.place: Chennai, final v Royal Challengers Bangalore
events.text: Murali Vijay's 95 and a 58-run win make Chennai the first team to defend the IPL title, in front of their home crowd at Chepauk.

events.title: 0–4 in England, and the Bell recall
events.text: The No.1 ranking is lost in a 0–4 whitewash. At Trent Bridge, Dhoni withdraws a run-out appeal against Ian Bell after tea, an act that wins him the ICC Spirit of Cricket award. A 0–4 defeat in Australia follows that winter.

events.title: Honorary Lieutenant Colonel
events.text: Conferred the honorary rank of Lieutenant Colonel in the Territorial Army's Parachute Regiment, alongside Abhinav Bindra. He completes five parachute jumps at Agra in 2015 to earn his para wings.

events.title: 224 against Australia
events.text: His highest first-class score, 224 off 265 balls, is the highest by an Indian captain in Tests at the time and the first Test double-century by an Indian wicketkeeper. India go on to win the series 4–0, their first whitewash of Australia.

events.title: Champions Trophy — the treble complete
events.text: Rain cuts the final to 20 overs a side. India make 129/7; England need 28 off 18 and Ishant Sharma takes Morgan and Bopara in one over before Jadeja and Ashwin close it out by five runs. Dhoni becomes the only captain to win the World T20, the World Cup and the Champions Trophy. India go through unbeaten.

events.title: 15 off the last over, Port of Spain
events.text: Back from injury, batting with the last man, India need 15 off Shaminda Eranga's final over. Dhoni hits 6, 4, 6 and finishes 45 not out off 52 balls. A finisher's template in three balls.

events.title: World T20 final lost to Sri Lanka
events.text: India reach the final unbeaten but make only 130/4; Sri Lanka chase it with 13 balls to spare. It is Dhoni's second ICC final defeat as captain after the 2009 Champions Trophy exit.

events.title: Retires from Test cricket
events.place: Melbourne, after the third Test v Australia
events.text: Minutes after a draw at the MCG he announces his retirement from Tests with one match of the series left. He leaves as India's most successful Test captain (27 wins in 60) with 4,876 runs and 294 dismissals; Virat Kohli takes over at Sydney.

events.title: World Cup semi-final, Sydney
events.text: India win all seven matches before the semi-final, the first time a side has taken all 70 wickets on offer through the group stage. Chasing 329 they fall 95 short; Dhoni makes 65. Ziva Dhoni is born in Ranchi on 6 February, mid-tournament, while he is away.

events.title: Asia Cup, now a T20 event
events.text: India beat Bangladesh by eight wickets, Dhoni finishing with 20 not out off 6 balls. Two weeks later at the World T20 in Bengaluru he runs out Mustafizur Rahman off the last ball, glove already off, to win by one run.

events.title: Steps down as limited-overs captain
events.text: Two days before the squad for England is picked he hands the ODI and T20I captaincy to Virat Kohli, saying he will remain available as a player. His last series as captain was the home ODIs against New Zealand in October 2016, won 3–2.

events.title: Padma Bhushan, in uniform
events.text: He receives India's third-highest civilian award from President Ram Nath Kovind dressed in his Territorial Army uniform, saluting before accepting it.

events.title: CSK return and win the IPL
events.text: After a two-year suspension Chennai come back with the oldest squad in the league and win it. Dhoni makes 455 runs at a strike rate of 150; Shane Watson's 117 not out settles the final.

events.title: 10,000 ODI runs
events.text: He becomes the fourth Indian and the first Indian wicketkeeper to 10,000 ODI runs. Only Sangakkara and Gilchrist among keepers had passed the mark, and neither at his average.

events.title: Last international innings
events.place: Old Trafford, World Cup semi-final v New Zealand
events.text: India are 24/4 chasing 240 across two days. Dhoni and Jadeja add 116. With 25 needed off 10, Dhoni hits Lockie Ferguson for six, then is run out for 50 by Martin Guptill's direct hit from the deep. He does not play for India again.

events.title: 19:29 — retires from international cricket
events.text: A video montage set to 'Main pal do pal ka shayar hoon', captioned: 'Thanks a lot for ur love and support throughout. from 1929 hrs consider me as retired.' He never publicly explained the time. He is 39, has not played for India in 13 months and is in Dubai preparing for IPL 2020.

events.title: Fourth IPL title
events.place: Dubai, final v Kolkata Knight Riders
events.text: A year after CSK's first bottom-half finish, they win the title in the UAE by 27 runs. Dhoni's 18 off 6 in the Qualifier against Delhi, the match that got them there, is the finisher at 40.

events.title: Fifth title, on one knee
events.text: Playing the whole season on a damaged left knee, he leads CSK to a fifth title, level with Rohit Sharma's Mumbai Indians. Ravindra Jadeja hits 6 and 4 off the last two balls; Dhoni has surgery days later. It is his tenth IPL final as captain.

events.title: ICC Hall of Fame
events.text: Inducted into the ICC Hall of Fame alongside Hashim Amla, Matthew Hayden, Graeme Smith, Daniel Vettori, Sarah Taylor and Sana Mir. The ICC's citation records 538 matches, 17,266 runs and the only captaincy treble of ICC white-ball trophies.

events.title: Captain again, at 43
events.text: When Ruturaj Gaikwad breaks his elbow he takes CSK's captaincy back for the rest of a season in which Chennai finish bottom for the first time. He is the oldest player in the league and still keeping wicket.
